picks.title: Five AI tools for prostate cancer screening are recommended by NICE
picks.excerpt: NICE has recommended five AI tools that highlight areas of possible prostate cancer on MRI for NHS use while further evidence on their accuracy is generated.
picks.rationale: A regulator decision: NICE cleared five prostate-MRI AI tools for NHS use while evidence is gathered. The 10-14 AuntMinnie card was a single accuracy study, not a health-technology appraisal, so this is a separate event.

picks.title: Can AI diagnose like a team of doctors? New research puts it to the test
picks.excerpt: Microsoft AI published new research testing whether its diagnostic orchestrator can work through complex cases like a panel of doctors, claiming it outperforms physicians on diagnostic accuracy.
picks.rationale: New diagnostic-orchestrator research from Microsoft AI, benchmarked against physician panels. Microsoft has no card in the 30-day history. The accuracy figures are the vendor's own claims, so the enrichment pass should attribute them.

picks.title: Human oversight of erroneous clinical AI and decision support: a systematic review and meta-analysis
picks.excerpt: Artificial intelligence (AI) increasingly supports clinical decisions, but human oversight is protective only if clinicians recognize and resist erroneous output. We systematically reviewed controlled and real-world studies of clinician responses to incorrect automated advice. Forty-six reports repr
picks.rationale: A meta-analysis of 46 reports on whether clinicians catch wrong AI advice. It tests the 'human in the loop' assumption behind current regulation. The 10-21 card was one neonatal automation-bias study, and the tagged 10-19 BMJ match is a different systematic review on trial reporting.

picks.rationale: The Korean Pharmaceutical Association launched a practice-support AI for medication review and counselling and is recruiting pharmacists for field tests. It reaches front-line clinicians, and no pharmacy-AI story appears in the 30-day history.
